prompt:
This is a volleyball match. This clip begins at {start} seconds into the match and runs for {length} seconds.

List every serve, receive, set, dig, attack, kill and block you see. Follow these logging rules:
- Do not log routine sets during a rally; only log a set if it directly precedes a point-winning kill.
- Only log a block if it is a stuff block that directly ends the rally; do not log block jumps or soft block deflections where play continues.
- Never log both an attack and a kill for the same hit: if the spike wins the point, log it only as a kill; otherwise log it as an attack.
- Only log a dig when a defender successfully keeps an opponent's attack in play; never log a failed defensive touch or shank after a point-winning kill.
- Follow the contact sequence within each team possession: the 1st touch after an opponent's attack is a dig, the 2nd touch (only before a kill) is a set, and the final touch sending the ball over the net is an attack or kill; never log a dig on a teammate's touch or two attacks in the same possession.

For each one give:
  t      - the time in absolute match seconds (clip start {start} + offset)
  type   - serve, receive, set, dig, attack, kill or block
  side   - "left" or "right" of the net
  number - the player's shirt number, or null
  error  - true if it was an error
  point  - true if it won the point
diff: This is a volleyball match. This clip begins at {start} seconds into the match and runs for {length} seconds.
List every serve, receive, set, dig, attack, kill and block you see. Follow these logging rules:
- Do not log routine sets during a rally; only log a set if it directly precedes a point-winning kill.
- Only log a block if it is a stuff block that directly ends the rally; do not log block jumps or soft block deflections where play continues.
- Never log both an attack and a kill for the same hit: if the spike wins the point, log it only as a kill; otherwise log it as an attack.
- Only log a dig when a defender successfully keeps an opponent's attack in play; never log a failed defensive touch or shank after a point-winning kill.

- Follow the contact sequence within each team possession: the 1st touch after an opponent's attack is a dig, the 2nd touch (only before a kill) is a set, and the final touch sending the ball over the net is an attack or kill; never log a dig on a teammate's touch or two attacks in the same possession.
t      - the time in absolute match seconds (clip start {start} + offset)
type   - serve, receive, set, dig, attack, kill or block
number - the player's shirt number, or null
error  - true if it was an error
point  - true if it won the point
conjecture: The error log shows the model frequently confuses contact roles within a single team's possession—calling a first-contact dig a set (2971.73), calling a second-contact set an attack (3129.04) or dig (1460.00), and logging impossible same-team sequences like attack -> dig -> attack (1918.92-1922.02) or consecutive attacks by the same player (3129.04, 3130.24). Adding a rule that enforces volleyball's within-possession contact sequence (1st contact after crossing the net is receive/dig, 2nd is set before a kill, 3rd is attack/kill, with at most one dig and one attack/kill per team possession) will eliminate same-team duplicate touches and role swaps.
prediction: Same-team duplicate attacks and digs drop by ~20 and dig/set/attack role swaps drop by ~6, reducing invented events to ~95 and raising OVERALL F1 by +0.020.

lessons.text:
- Suppressing routine in-rally sets to only log sets that directly assist a point-winning kill works best as a foundational rule, cutting invented events to 230 and boosting OVERALL F1 by +0.080 over the 0.621 baseline (gen_01/cand_0, mean 0.701).
- Enforcing mutual exclusivity between 'attack' and 'kill' and restricting 'block' to rally-ending stuff blocks works strongly, cutting invented events from 230 to 150 and raising mean OVERALL F1 by +0.034 (gen_02/cand_0, 0.701 to 0.735; also +0.039 over baseline alone in gen_01/cand_1).
- Restricting 'dig' to successful defensive saves on opposing spikes and forbidding defensive touches after a point-winning kill works well, cutting invented events from 150 to 117 and raising mean OVERALL F1 by +0.024 (gen_03/cand_0, 0.735 to 0.759).
- Stacking action-pruning rules sequentially across generations (sets in gen 1 -> blocks/kills in gen 2 -> digs in gen 3) compounds gains cleanly, reducing invented events by more than half (from >230 to 117) and raising mean OVERALL F1 by +0.138 total (0.621 to 0.759).
- Clarifying that deflected point-winning spikes are still rally-ending 'kills' and excluding soft free-ball passes from 'attacks' reached the highest single-run F1 of 0.777 (103 invented) and a 2-run mean of 0.766 (+0.007 over gen_03/cand_0), though it was rejected on confirmation (gen_04/cand_3).
- Providing team jersey colors and valid roster numbers trades action/time precision for shirt number accuracy: in every generation it boosted number F1 (+0.014 in gen_02/cand_3, +0.043 in gen_03/cand_3, +0.019 in gen_04/cand_0) but degraded time/action F1 and increased invented events (e.g., 117 to 133 in gen_04/cand_0, dropping OVERALL F1 from 0.766 to 0.753).
- Attempting to fix early serve timestamps via prompt instructions consistently fails to improve OVERALL F1 across all four generations, whether anchored to physical ball-hand contact (gen_01/cand_3: 0.653; gen_02/cand_2: 0.688), ~1s before receive (gen_03/cand_2: 0.736), or crossing the net (gen_04/cand_1: 0.752 vs 0.759 baseline).
- Restricting 'attack' and 'kill' strictly to "jumping overhead hits" trades fewer invented events for worse recall, cutting inventions from 150 to 132 but increasing missed events from 39 to 46 and leaving OVERALL F1 flat at 0.735 (gen_03/cand_1).
- Adding multi-contact sequence logic for digs (forbidding consecutive digs or digs by the attacking team) does not improve over simpler dig rules, slightly increasing invented events (117 to 121) and missed events (33 to 37) for an OVERALL F1 of 0.761 (gen_04/cand_2).
- Ordering of rules matters for evaluation efficiency: applying dig restrictions in gen 3 after block/kill cleanup yielded a kept +0.024 mean gain (gen_03/cand_0), whereas applying it in gen 2 before block/kill cleanup yielded a smaller single-run score of 0.716 and was rejected (gen_02/cand_1).
- Open question: Since in-prompt roster constraints repeatedly degraded action and time detection (gen_01/cand_2, gen_02/cand_3, gen_03/cand_3, gen_04/cand_0), can jersey numbers be constrained or mapped in a deterministic post-processing step to capture the +0.043 number F1 gain without hurting event detection?
- Open question: Can the two components of gen_04/cand_3 (counting deflected winning spikes as rally-ending kills vs. excluding free balls from attacks) be tested separately to isolate which rule drove the drop to 103 invented events and the 0.777 peak score?
- Open question: Since prompt instructions failed to fix the systematic 1.1s–1.7s early bias on serves across four attempts, would a deterministic post-processing timestamp shift (+1.0s on predicted serves) recover those ~12–16 missed serves without disrupting model inference?
